rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an's small verbal differences are intentional in every detail and display the highest artistry, rhetoric, and inimitability.
rows.anchor: في القرآن الكريم آيات وتعبيرات تتشابه مع تعبيرات أخرى ولا تختلف عنها إلا في مواطن ضئيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿImrān uses Bakka in the pilgrimage context, echoing bakk, crowding; al-Fatḥ uses the familiar Makka where crowding is not the point, and both explanations may apply.
rows.anchor: وسبب إيرادها بالباء في آل عمران أن الآية في سياق الحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Nisāʾ says to show good after condemning public evil; al-Aḥzāb says to show anything because its context stresses God's knowledge of what is hidden and manifest.
rows.anchor: أي: إن تُظهروا خيراً، هو عكس الجهر بالسوء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrah usage also favors the choices: khayr occurs twelve times in al-Nisāʾ and twice in al-Aḥzāb; shayʾ occurs twelve and six times, respectively.
rows.anchor: ذلك أن كلمة (خير) ترددت في سورة النساء اثنتي عشرة مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Baqarah uses akbar in 2:217 amid repeated language of great matters, while 2:191 depicts severity against disbelievers and therefore uses ashadd.
rows.anchor: وذلك لأن الكلام في الآية الثانية على كبيرات الأمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah says māl in Hūd because the next statement mentions God's treasuries; elsewhere Noah and other prophets say ajr, since خزائن fits مال especially well.
rows.anchor: وسبب ذلك أنه في الموضع الذي وردت فيه كلمة (مال)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Naḥl uses the masculine pronoun for the subset of livestock that yields milk; al-Muʾminūn uses the feminine for all livestock, whose many benefits are then listed.
rows.anchor: فلما كانت الأنعام في الآية الثانية أكثر جاء بالضمير الدال على الكثرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites an Arabic pattern in which masculine agreement can signal a smaller group, while feminine agreement can signal a larger group.
rows.anchor: وذلك نحو قوله تعالى: {وَقَالَ نِسْوَةٌ} [يوسف: 30]

rows.speaker: درة التنزيل
rows.claim: Durrat al-Tanzīl says al-anʿām in 16:66 denotes only some livestock because milk comes from some females; in 23:21–22 the broader benefits require all kinds.
rows.anchor: جاء في (درة التنزيل) في هاتين الآيتين:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After mentioning the sending of tranquility and increase in believers' faith, al-Fatḥ 4 ends with God's knowledge and wisdom, which suit that context.
rows.anchor: فهذا موضع عِلْمٍ وحكمة فقال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After threats and punishment for hypocrites and polytheists, al-Fatḥ 7 names God mighty and wise, fitting a context of power, victory, and judgment.
rows.anchor: فهذا موضع عِزَّةٍ وغَلَبة وحكم فقال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author initially regarded claims of the Qur'an's inimitability as exaggeration driven by religious zeal, and many stylistic explanations as forced or unscientific.
rows.anchor: وكنت آرى في هذا غلواً ومبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After reading widely in language, exegesis, inimitability, and rhetoric, he began accepting the claim, while still considering much writing unconvincing.
rows.anchor: بدأت أميل إلى تصديق هذه المقولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His own comparisons of Qur'anic wording, order, omission, and other features convinced him that every word, letter, and vowel is calculated and that the Qur'an cannot be human speech.
rows.anchor: وجدت تعبيراً فنياً مقصوداً حُسِبَ لكل كلمة فيه حسابُها بل لكل حرف بل لكل حركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He offers the book as a guide to some linguistic artistry, admits he may not be free of bias, and invites readers to examine it open-mindedly and patiently rather than accept assertions.
rows.anchor: وهذا الكتاب أحسبه من هذا النمط فما هو إلا دليل يشير إلى شيء من مواطن الفن والجمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afnān encompasses several kinds of blessing, making the first pair's description superior; mudhāmmatān means darkened toward black by intense greenness.
rows.anchor: والوصف الأول أعلى فإن الأفنان تطلق على ضروب عدة من النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The upper gardens' flowing water is more abundant than the lower gardens' gushing water.
rows.anchor: وماء الجري أكثر من ماء النضخ

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported view is that flowing springs convey additional qualities of blessing that the description 'gushing' does not.
rows.anchor: وقيل في الجري معان أخرى من صفات النعم لا يفيدها قوله نضاختان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The upper gardens contain every kind of fruit in pairs, an inclusive description beyond the lower gardens' named fruit, date palms, and pomegranates.
rows.anchor: العليين. من كل فاكهة زوجين على سبيل الاستغراق والعموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the upper gardens he mentions only brocade linings, omitting the outer surfaces to signal their elevation and the limits of description; the lower gardens are described directly.
rows.anchor: فقد ذكر بطائن الأولى فقال: إنها من استبرق

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf infers that if the linings are brocade, the outer surfaces must be grander still.
rows.anchor: قال في (الكشاف) : "وإذا كانت البطائن من إستبرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The upper gardens' women are described by the active participle qāṣirāt, while the lower gardens use the passive maqṣūrāt; Samarrāʾī says this marks a difference in rank.
rows.anchor: فانظر هداك الله وصف (القاصرات) بصيغة اسم الفاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The upper gardens' women are likened to ruby and coral, a description omitted for the lower gardens that encourages striving for good deeds and their reward.
rows.anchor: وهذا الوصف مدعاة إلى التشويق لإحسان العمل

rows.speaker: السلف الصالح
rows.claim: The author attributes to the early righteous scholars the count of eight refrain repetitions for each garden matching Paradise's eight gates, and seven in Hell after 55:31 matching its seven gates.
rows.anchor: ذكرها السلف الصالح رضوان الله عليهم، وهي أن قوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Samarrāʾī identifies the foremost, brought-near ones as the highest of creation and contrasts their reward with that of the companions of the right.
rows.anchor: في التفريق بين نعيم السابقين المقربين وهم أعلى الخلق ونعيم أصحاب اليمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The foremost recline on gold-woven couches facing one another; the companions of the right receive raised beds, a visibly lower description.
rows.anchor: ذكر أن السابقين على سُرُرٍ مَّوْضُونَةٍ وهي المشبكة بالذهب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative reported interpretation takes the raised beds to mean women.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنَّ المراد بالفرش ههنا النساء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The foremost are served by immortal youths with cups, pitchers, and a flowing drink; the companions of the right are instead described with poured water.
rows.anchor: وذكر أن السابقين يطوف علبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The foremost choose whatever fruit and bird meat they desire, while the companions of the right are described with sidr, talh, and abundant fruit.
rows.anchor: وذكر نعيم السابقين فقال: {وَفَاكِهَةٍ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The foremost are explicitly promised houris like hidden pearls; the companions' women are described as newly created virgins, like the women likened to ruby and coral in al-Raḥmān.
rows.anchor: وذكر أزواج السابقين من الحور العين فقال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrasts show that Qur'anic wording follows meaning and circumstance across an individual verse, a sūrah, and the Qur'an as a whole, supporting the challenge to produce its like.
rows.anchor: وأن التشابه والاختلاف في قسم من التعبيرات إنما يقتضيه المعنى والمقام
